title: Cyborg Roaches Could Be the Future of Triage Medicine - Nautilus
gist: Australian engineers have turned the giant burrowing cockroach—the world's heaviest—into 'cyborg paramedics' that could deliver life-saving care to disaster victims trapped under rubble.

insights.claim: Australian engineers developed a way to transform giant burrowing cockroaches into cyborg mini-paramedics, publishing the results in Advanced Science.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: An early biohybrid-robotics application aimed at search-and-rescue triage—a niche to watch in disaster tech.
insights.locator: Australian engineers developed a way to transform these beefy bugs

insights.claim: The augmented insects are envisioned to deliver life-saving care to disaster victims, such as people buried beneath rubble.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Frames the intended use case—reaching victims inaccessible to human rescuers.
insights.locator: could deliver life-saving care to disaster victims

insights.claim: The giant burrowing cockroach is the world's heaviest cockroach and can grow over three inches long, making it a robust platform for augmentation.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Explains why this species is suited to carry payloads for the cyborg-paramedic concept.
